Q1: Diazinon is characterized by several known significant hazards, classified as Tier 1 based on the Globally Harmonized System (GHS), including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, environmental, oral, dermal/eye, and organ/systemic effects. Furthermore, it presents Tier 2 hazards for endocrine disruption and inhalation, drawing on a broader scientific perspective beyond GHS to provide a more comprehensive view of its potential risks.
Q2: Diazinon appears on several significant 'Lists of Concern,' including classification as a Group 2A carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) and being identified as a potential endocrine disruptor by the TEDX list. It is also regulated under the Clean Water Act, Safe Drinking Water Act, and EPA's Drinking Water Standard, reflecting its recognized environmental and public health impacts as a pesticide.
Q3: Diazinon is very well characterized; with 16,000 literature references, its depth of study far exceeds the typical chemical. Its precise molecular formula and 'Small Molecule' classification, along with the absence of any data deficient (Tier 4) hazard categories, confirm it is a clearly defined and extensively researched substance.
